Alice —

Appreciate the quick review and the flagged concerns. High level: Redwood's standard commercial DPA tries to balance operational realities with customers' need for rapid notification. Below are our proposed positions; I can circulate a redline if we converge on the approach.

1) Initial notification timing
- Confirmed incidents that materially affect a customer's data: initial notification within 48 hours of confirmation.
- For incidents that are confirmed as "critical / high-severity" (e.g., confirmed exfiltration of customer PII), we will use commercially reasonable efforts to notify within 24 hours of confirmation and will prioritize escalation paths.
- For suspected incidents where scope is unknown, we commit to an initial "acknowledgement" within 24 hours and a substantive update within 48-72 hours as investigations progress.

2) Evidence preservation and access
- Redwood will preserve forensic logs, relevant snapshots, and chain-of-custody artifacts for a minimum of 90 days by default.
- For customers with regulatory obligations, we can agree to preserve evidence for up to 180 days on request (subject to reasonable cost recovery for extraordinary export volumes).

3) Cross-border handling and regulator assistance
- Redwood will assist with cross-border evidence transfers where required for regulator engagement, using standard safeguards (SCCs where applicable, additional safeguards on a case-by-case basis).
- We propose language that commits to cooperation with lawful regulator requests and to notify the customer before transferring evidence outside the EU unless prohibited by law.

4) Subprocessors and notices
- We will provide an up-to-date list of subprocessors within 10 business days of request and include subprocessors in incident investigations where they materially relate to the event.

If that framing is acceptable, I'll prepare a redline for your team. I've attached a draft notice wording that we often use (Redwood-notice-language_v1.docx) — feel free to mark it up.

Priya — quick operational take: 

- 24-hour mandatory notice for "critical" incidents: feasible, but only if the customer provides a named 24/7 contact and we have an agreed escalation path. Our on-call SREs can mobilize and provide an initial substantive update within 24 hours in most cases, but confirmation of scope often takes longer. We should keep the "24-hour initial notice for critical incidents" and couple it with a follow-up timeline (e.g., 48-72 hours for scope).

- Evidence extraction & delivery: we can produce exports within ~7-10 business days for most requests. For very large artifacts (multi-TB) or complex chain-of-custody needs, we should reserve the right to charge for retrieval and courier costs. Suggest we include: (i) a reasonable cost-recovery clause; (ii) a mechanism to estimate costs within 5 business days of request; (iii) a cap for standard requests (e.g., up to 50 GB at no charge).

- 12-month retention: operationally expensive and storage-intensive if applied broadly. Recommend: 90 days default, 180 days for subscription add-on / contract tier, and 12 months only for named regulated customers where Redwood and customer agree to additional fees. That fits our storage and compliance roadmap.

- Cross-border transfers: we support SCCs and will work with Legal on exporter/importer roles. We need the contract to allow us to comply with lawful disclosure requests and to notify the customer when possible.

Happy to provide sample wording for the ops/cost clauses. From an SRE perspective, the proposed compromise Priya outlined is reasonable.

Priya / Marcus — thanks for the input. Legal position and proposed final redline below: 

Proposed contract language (high-level):
1) Notification timing
- Redwood shall provide initial written notification to Customer without undue delay and, in any event, within forty-eight (48) hours of Redwood's confirmation that an Incident has materially affected Customer Data.
- For Incidents Redwood classifies as "Critical" (defined in the DPA as incidents involving confirmed unauthorized access to or exfiltration of Customer PII or other regulated data), Redwood shall provide initial written notification within twenty-four (24) hours of such classification, provided Customer has supplied a 24/7 priority contact and escalation details.

2) Evidence preservation and access
- Redwood will preserve relevant forensic artifacts and access logs for a minimum of ninety (90) days by default.
- Redwood will extend preservation to one hundred eighty (180) days for Customers who contract for the higher retention tier. Requests for preservation beyond 180 days (including requests up to 12 months) may be accommodated where agreed in writing and are subject to reasonable cost recovery.
- Upon receipt of a duly executed NDA and written request, Redwood will make reasonable efforts to provide copies of requested forensic artifacts within ten (10) business days for standard requests (up to 50 GB). For larger or extraordinary requests, Redwood will provide a cost estimate within five (5) business days and use commercially reasonable efforts to comply.

3) Cross-border transfers and regulator assistance
- Redwood will cooperate with Customer and applicable regulators in cross-border investigations, using SCCs or other appropriate transfer mechanisms where transfers are necessary. Redwood will, to the extent permitted by law, notify Customer prior to transferring data outside the EEA.

4) Subprocessors
- Redwood will provide an up-to-date list of subprocessors upon request within ten (10) business days and will include materially relevant subprocessors in remediation coordination for incidents that involve those subprocessors.

5) Exceptions and good faith efforts
- Where Redwood is legally prohibited from notifying Customer or transferring evidence (e.g., under a law enforcement or national security order), Redwood will use reasonable efforts to comply with applicable legal constraints and will notify Customer when permitted.

I think the language above reflects an appropriate commercial compromise — it creates clear contractual commitments while preserving operational protections. Priya, please send this redline to Fintegral and propose a short call if they push back on the retention numbers.
